payload.rationale: The Chargers host the Raiders at SoFi Stadium in Week 2. Observed facts: Raiders are 1-0 (27-13 win), Chargers 0-1 (14-26 loss); Raiders' star TE Brock Bowers is doubtful and CB Darien Porter is out, while the Chargers are missing OL Trey Pipkins and DB Elijah Molden with WR Ladd McConkey questionable. Transfer assumptions from general background: the Chargers were a playoff-caliber roster with a franchise QB and an established coaching staff in the prior season, while the Raiders were a rebuilding team with a much worse record; that prior-season gap, plus home-field advantage (~2-3 points), typically outweighs a single week of results. Week 1 outcomes are noisy and carry only modest predictive weight, though they do slightly narrow the gap. Bowers' likely absence meaningfully hurts the Raiders' offense. Netting these, I estimate the Chargers win roughly 63-66% of the time, with ~0.3% tie probability (a tie is not a YES). Too high: the Raiders' Week 1 dominance and the Chargers' flat opener could reflect real 2026 roster changes I cannot observe (offseason turnover, QB situations), and divisional games are often closer than talent gaps imply. Too low: if the Chargers remain the clear roster-quality favorite and Bowers sits, home favorites of that caliber often win closer to 70%; Week 1 results may be largely opponent-driven noise.
limitations: Only one 2026 game per team observed; no opponent-adjusted strength ratings supplied.
Prior-season team quality is a transfer assumption; 2026 offseason roster and coaching changes are unknown to me.
Injury designations may change before kickoff; final inactive list not available.
Tie (~0.3%) settles at 0.50, not YES; estimate is win probability only.
